answer.label: Attributed to
answer.authorDates: b. 22 November 1943 · 39-time Grand Slam tennis champion
answer.sourceLine: Credited to King on every major quote site — Goodreads, BrainyQuote and AZQuotes — and fully consistent with her competitive creed. But none cite a book, speech or interview, the line is absent from her memoirs, and no primary source pins it to her.

source.heading: The trail of an unsourced line

docMeta.dd: “Champions keep playing until they get it right.”

source.excerpt: Champions keep playing until they get it right.
trail: Every major quote site — Goodreads, BrainyQuote, AZQuotes — runs the line under King’s name with no book, date or interview attached.
AZQuotes tags it a ‘Twitter post from Jan 26, 2015,’ but links to no actual tweet and offers no earlier source.
King’s genuinely documented maxim is a different line — “pressure is a privilege” — the title of her 2008 book with Christine Brennan.
source.excerptNote: This is the whole line as it circulates — a free-standing aphorism with no surrounding passage, because no original context (a book page, a speech, a transcript) has ever been produced for it.
source.rightsNote: Treated as a modern, still-in-copyright saying: if it is King’s, it is a late-20th/early-21st-century line, not public domain. Because no source is verified, reuse should say “attributed to” rather than assert authorship.

author.name: Billie Jean King
author.heading: About Billie Jean King
author.metaLine: b. 1943 · 39-time Grand Slam champion, equality advocate
author.bio: Billie Jean King (born 22 November 1943, Long Beach, California) is an American tennis champion who won 39 Grand Slam titles and beat Bobby Riggs in the 1973 Battle of the Sexes. A lifelong advocate for equal pay and women’s sport, she is famous for pithy competitive maxims — most reliably “pressure is a privilege,” the title of her 2008 book. Her genuine phrasing is well documented; this particular line is not.

context.heading: Why the attribution sticks
lead: The line rides on a real reputation. Billie Jean King is genuinely quotable about grit and pressure, so a maxim about champions who “keep playing until they get it right” sounds exactly like something she would say — which is precisely why it spread under her name without anyone stopping to ask where she said it.

The tell is uniformity without evidence: dozens of sites repeat the identical wording and the identical author, yet not one cites a book page, a match, a speech or a dated interview. That pattern — total agreement, zero sourcing — is the fingerprint of an aggregator-propagated attribution rather than a documented one.
context.detailsSummary: What King is actually on record saying
detailsBody: Her documented competitive creed is “pressure is a privilege” — a phrase she used for decades and made the title of her 2008 book with Christine Brennan. That line has a paper trail; this one does not, which is why we log it as attributed rather than verified.
context.pull: Total agreement, zero sourcing — the fingerprint of an aggregator quote.
